transcript.text: Apologies for the unclear input earlier. Let me address both questions directly. First, on the collateral gap: the $4,000,000 in eligible unencumbered Treasury bills I identified is what we have confirmed as eligible for the rail's liquidity facility today. The modeled peak two-hour net outflow of $6.5M that Jonas shared exceeds that by $2.5M. From a liquidity risk perspective, I cannot recommend activation until that gap is bridged — either by committing additional eligible collateral to the rail's liquidity facility or by treasury allocating supplementary liquidity resources. That determination and the sizing of any additional buffer would need to come from Maya as the binding treasury decision-maker, but my risk assessment is that $4M against a $6.5M modeled peak — which Jonas noted is not even a stress scenario — leaves us exposed. Second, on monitoring: the daily eligibility and substitution check our policy requires is necessary but not sufficient for an instant-payments rail. Given that settlement is continuous and intraday, I recommend we also implement intraday monitoring of collateral eligibility and utilization. Jonas's proposed real-time settlement position tracking with threshold alerts at 50% and 75% of the committed buffer is a good foundation, and I'd ask that those alerts also trigger a real-time check of remaining eligible collateral against the current net outflow position. This way, if outflows accelerate, we have an early warning not just on the cash side but on the collateral side as well. I'd also note that the inventory note documenting the $4M in eligible collateral still needs to be attached to the operating-plan file, and I'll ensure that happens before any sign-off.
